title: Sententiarum Ex Operibus Augustini Delibatarum Liber Unus
author: Prosperus Aquitanus
source: Translated by Claude from tmp834.tmp834.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.

passages.original: Ut recte credatur Pater et Filius, ipse Filius audiendus est, dicens, Ego et Pater unum sumus (Joan. X, 30). Duobus enim verbis duae simul hæreses detruncantur. Nam per id quod ait, unum, Arium perculit : per illud quod ait, sumus, Sabellium stravit : quia nec, sumus, de uno, nec, unum c diceret de diverso (Aug. ibid., n. 9).
passages.english: For the Father and the Son to be rightly believed in, the Son himself must be heard, saying, "I and the Father are one" (John 10:30). For by two words two heresies are cut down at once. For by saying "one" he struck down Arius; by saying "are" he laid Sabellius low: because he would neither say "are" of one [person], nor "one" of what is diverse (Aug., ibid., n. 9).
passages.notes: The stray "c" after "unum" is taken as a footnote mark and omitted. "Diverso" is rendered "what is diverse", that is, of things differing in nature.
